items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: Floyd Campbell had a piano player, that who had formerly played with me, with us in Jackson, Tennessee, named Gus Perryman.

ctx.x: No, Gus was a trombone player. He could play piano. Trombone player. And he was an kind-of arranger. And he was a modern arranger back in those days. He could write like mad. But he was the type of guy if you said, "Gus, that was a beautiful (unintelligible) solo," he'd get up and walk off the bandstand because he'd think you was trying to jive him, you know, kid him. And he had that little mental problem, see. And he left his mother -- his father had died, and his mother lived up in Des Moines, Iowa, I think.…

Well, I have nothing but pleasant memories being around him because he knew music, and he was a genius. But there was just something about him that he just -- he just couldn't make it. He just couldn't make it. It was a tragic thing about his life.
